risks.note: Energy expenditure constitutes a material component of cement manufacturing costs and a significant source of greenhouse gas emissions; escalating energy prices, regulatory momentum toward low-carbon operations and the cement sector's net-zero-by-2070 commitment require sustained efficiency gains and a transition to cleaner energy. Financial implication flagged as negative.

Water is an essential input across cement, tiles and ready-mixed concrete operations; intensifying water stress, competition for freshwater and heightened regulatory oversight demand structured water stewardship. Mitigated through ZLD across plants under operational control, rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge.

Emissions from manufacturing can adversely affect ambient air quality in surrounding areas and expose the Company to regulatory sanctions and reputational consequences, while quarrying and manufacturing can affect local ecosystems and habitats, putting the social licence to operate and evolving disclosure requirements at stake; addressed through CEMS/CAAQMS monitoring, LEAP-based biodiversity risk assessments, TNFD alignment and mine rehabilitation.
risks.risk: Air quality and biodiversity impact of quarrying and manufacturing

risks.note: Unsafe working environments expose employees, contractors and workers to injury risks and the Company to regulatory penalties, legal liability and reputational harm; managed through an OHS policy and management system across all sites and periodic risk assessments.

Inability to attract, develop and retain a skilled workforce can widen capability gaps, dampen productivity and constrain execution of the strategic growth agenda; unresolved labour grievances and inadequate worker engagement can precipitate industrial action and disrupt production continuity.
risks.risk: Talent attraction, retention and labour relations

risks.note: Non-adherence to regulatory and statutory obligations can give rise to legal penalties, operational disruptions and loss of stakeholder confidence; breaches of ethical conduct and deficiencies in governance structures can inflict lasting reputational damage and trigger regulatory action; and inadequate data governance and privacy safeguards can result in significant regulatory fines, reputational damage and operational disruption.
risks.risk: Regulatory and statutory compliance, governance, ethics and data protection

risks.note: The Company is exposed to credit risk on trade receivables (treated as in default when payments are more than 2 years past due, with an expected credit loss allowance), liquidity risk in meeting financial liabilities as they fall due, and market risk comprising foreign exchange exposure from overseas sales, purchases and foreign currency loans as well as interest rate risk.
risks.risk: Financial risks - credit, liquidity and market risk

risks.note: Unsustainable or unethical supplier conduct - human rights violations, environmental non-compliance or governance failures - can precipitate supply chain disruptions and reputational harm; unaddressed human rights risks in sourcing, contracting and employment can erode stakeholder trust and attract regulatory scrutiny.
risks.risk: Supply chain and supplier sustainability, including human rights
